introduction.situation: Physics studies matter, radiation and fields across a very wide range of system sizes, from elementary particles to the whole universe.
introduction.complication: The existing groups are scattered across overlapping schemes based on constants, source headings and teaching categories, so the same scale appears in many places.
introduction.question: At which scale of system does each topic of physics belong?
introduction.answer: Physics is divided by the scale of the system studied: subatomic, atomic and optical, condensed and soft matter, plasmas and fluids, and gravitational and cosmic.

governing_thought: Physics is divided by the scale of the system studied: subatomic, atomic and optical, condensed and soft matter, plasmas and fluids, and gravitational and cosmic.

key_line.mece_dimension: the scale of the system studied
key_line.rank_note: Ranked from the smallest systems to the largest; plasmas and fluids are placed by their continuum description.

field_check.governing_thought: Physics is divided by the scale of the system studied: subatomic, atomic and optical, condensed and soft matter, plasmas and fluids, and gravitational and cosmic.
key_line: The subatomic scale covers elementary particles, quantum fields and atomic nuclei.
The atomic, molecular and optical scale covers atoms, molecules, light and the quantum probes that resolve them.
The condensed and soft matter scale covers many-particle systems: phases, solids, liquids, electronic and magnetic materials, soft, living and network matter.
The plasma, fluid and continuum scale covers matter described as a continuous medium: flow, transport, waves, beams and plasmas.
The gravitational and cosmic scale covers gravity, relativity, stars, galaxies and the universe as a whole.
